proof:
# Integer centroid does not bound ambient volume by mixed volume

Even with one integer coordinate, exactly three positive full-dimensional
fibers, and the TRUE mixed centroid in the central integer fiber, the ratio

    vol_(d+1)(conv S) / vol_MI(S)

is not bounded by a constant independent of d. This rules out replacing
the integer sum by an ambient integral with a factor depending only on n,
even under the integer-centroid condition. It is not an OC counterexample.

Fix d>=2 and a real parameter 0<s<1. Put

    A=2s^(d-1)/(1-s^(d-1)),   B=2s/(1-s).

In R x R^d define the full-dimensional convex polytope

    C_s={ (z,x): -1<=z<=1,
            0<=x_1<=1+z+A,
            0<=x_i<=1-z+B for 2<=i<=d }.

All defining inequalities are linear. The box at every -1<z<1 has
strictly positive side lengths, so the polytope has ambient interior.
Its only integer fibers are the positive boxes at -1,0,1. Their volumes are

    w_-=A(2+B)^(d-1),
    w_0=(1+A)(1+B)^(d-1),
    w_+=(2+A)B^(d-1).

The identities A/(2+A)=s^(d-1) and B/(2+B)=s give w_-=w_+.
Hence the true integer-coordinate centroid is zero. The box centroids
are affine in z, so the true continuous centroid is exactly the centroid
of the middle box:

    g=((1+A)/2,(1+B)/2,...,(1+B)/2).

Thus (0,g) is the actual mixed centroid and belongs to S. No exponential
tilt or reweighting has been made.

Every real box section is the Minkowski interpolation of the two endpoint
boxes, coordinate by coordinate. Therefore C_s=conv(S), so there is no
unrecorded bulge coming from noninteger generators of the original body.

The mixed mass is M_s=w_0+2w_-. Ordinary Fubini gives the ambient volume

    V_s=integral_-1^1 (1+z+A)(1-z+B)^(d-1) dz
       =((2+A+B)/d)[(2+B)^d-B^d]
         -(1/(d+1))[(2+B)^(d+1)-B^(d+1)].

For each fixed d, these explicit expressions are continuous as s decreases
to zero, with M_s tending to one. Substitution into V_s gives

    lim_(s downarrow 0) V_s/M_s
       =2^(d+1)/[d(d+1)].

The latter sequence is unbounded as d increases. Thus, for any prescribed
constant K, first choose d with 2^(d+1)>K d(d+1), then choose sufficiently
small positive s. The strict inequality persists on an interval by the
displayed continuity, so s may be chosen rational. Every such selected
example still has three positive d-dimensional integer fibers and a
true mixed centroid of integer base.

The construction does not involve a limit in the proposed OC conclusion.
The limit is used only to select finite, strictly positive examples that
disprove the auxiliary volume-comparison bound. In fact (0,g) itself is
an OC center here: any containing ambient halfspace contains the middle
box centroid and at least one endpoint centroid, since the centroid graph
is affine. Ordinary Grunbaum in those two boxes gives cap mass at least
gamma_d(w_0+w_-)>=(gamma_d/2)M_s. The failure is precisely the attempted
substitution of ambient volume for mixed volume.
